title: Policy graph compiler: constraint simplifier, region heuristics, and graceful fallback verifier
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Refactor the policy engine intake and compile path to produce a canonical, strongly-typed policy graph that can be statically validated and executed by the router. Scope includes: (1) a constraint simplifier that reduces redundant/overlapping rules, (2) region-selection heuristics module that annotates nodes with affinity scores and deterministic tie-breakers, and (3) a graceful fallback verifier that checks model variant compatibility and produces synthesized fallback chains with explicit degradation metadata. Goal is to reduce runtime routing exceptions, make policy migration safe, and provide deterministic quality signals for rollout automation.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical IR is produced from existing DSL inputs with a JSON schema and type hints documented in the PRD.
Constraint simplifier removes >=90% of semantically redundant rules in sample corpora without changing intended routing for test fixtures.
Region heuristics annotate nodes with 'affinity_score' and 'tie_breaker' fields; deterministic outputs for same input order.
Fallback verifier detects incompatible model-variant pairs and emits human-readable remediation hints (e.g., quantization mismatch, kv-cache incompatibility).
Unit and integration tests cover edge cases: overlapping range rules, wildcard tiers, multi-region fallbacks, and missing variant mappings.
Migration path: safe migration mode that flags breaking policy changes and produces a 'compatibility delta' report that can be consumed by the Console rollout UI.
Benchmark: policy compile latency under 200ms for policy bundles up to 15k rules on CI machine class; no regressions in router runtime for common request QPS patterns.
